Evidence: 30mm rain in 10 mins, destroyed lupins, smashed sheep feeders. #SouthAustralia #Agriculture #Aletheia

ABC News reports on intense regional storms in South Australia that unexpectedly ravaged ripening crops after years of drought broke.

A fierce 10-minute hailstorm tore through Sandalwood and Lameroo, obliterating up to 50% of key lupin crops and smashing crucial infrastructure.

Hail damages crops in a matter of minutes ahead of bumper harvest

After battling years of drought, farmers in South Australia have been in good spirits as above-average rainfall has fallen this year. However, a flash of heavy rain and hail has left some properties counting their losses.

ABC Riverland

Topic:Storms

Severe storms hit parts of regional South Australia, including in the Riverland and Mallee, yesterday. (Supplied: Murray River Pix)

Crops and feeder troughs have been damaged by hail at a property in Sandalwood in South Australia's Mallee.

Western parts of the Riverland and Mallee received between 13 and 35 millimetres of rain late on Tuesday.

Property owners are assessing the damage.

South Australian farmers preparing for a record-breaking harvest have had their crops damaged by rain and hail in a matter of minutes.

About 30 millimetres of rain in just 10 minutes fell at Kamora Park Poll Merino Station in Sandalwood, about 175 kilometres east of Adelaide.

The station was also hit by hail that stripped some crops to stalks.

"We had a pretty excellent lupin crop right where it's come through on the corner of our property, and we're not sure, but we suspect at least 50 per cent or more might be damaged," stud principal Katelyn Boughen said.

"We've probably been trying to grow these lupins for about three years now to save us a bit of money."

Ms Boughen said the hail was up to a centimetre in diameter and looked like snow.

"We were out and about near the sheds and as soon as it hit the tin roof it almost sounded like little gunshots, just pinging," she said.

Lameroo in the Mallee also experienced intense storms, with locals reporting 35mm of rain and hail falling within an hour, flooding the main street.

Residents reported 20mm in Halidon and 16mm in Loxton.

The Bureau of Meteorology said western parts of the Riverland, parts of the Mid North, Murraylands and North East Pastoral District were most affected, with 22mm of rain at Ponderosa, 16mm at Mount Mary and 13mm at Bakara Well.

Years of drought were broken this year with above-average rainfall in many parts of the state.

It has boosted crops and spirits, with a record-breaking harvest expected for this year.

But the flash of severe weather has brought disappointment for some.

"We're at the mercy of Mother Nature, and every year I think there's probably something different to handle, but I guess that's the challenge of what we choose to do," Ms Boughen said.

Katelyn Boughen says the area normally does not get enough rainfall, so the downpour was shocking. (Supplied: Murray River Pix)

Ms Boughen's aunty, Anne Boughen, estimated about a quarter of the crop, around 400 hectares, at Kamora Park was lost in the weather event.

"There were huge gutters washed in the paddocks, and it's not only the crops that have been damaged, but the much-needed sheep feeders also smashed," she said.

"The trees are stripped, and there were leaves all over the road, along with the hail and the steam coming up off the road as well.

"I've never, ever seen anything like it before."
